title: Virginia Small Claims Warrant in Debt Information
description: Proposed, narrowly scoped legal-information workflow for a self-represented defendant who identifies a served Virginia General District Court Small Claims Division Warrant in Debt (Form DC-402).

jurisdiction.court: Virginia General District Court Small Claims Division
jurisdiction.jurisdiction_notes: Only a served Form DC-402 small-claims Warrant in Debt is in scope; all other courts, forms, and procedures are excluded.

scope.purpose: Help a user identify the official form and court, organize the form's stated information, understand the official return-date process, and prepare user-directed questions and an outline without deciding a response.
includes: Explain source-supported terms on Form DC-402.
Help the user identify the court, case number, return date, claim amount, and stated claim basis.
Explain that the official form says a judgment may be entered if the defendant does not appear.
Offer a user-directed checklist and official source links.
excludes: Deciding whether the user should admit, deny, contest, remove, settle, or assert a defense.
Calculating a deadline or deciding whether service was valid.
Completing, signing, filing, serving, or submitting a document.
Giving advice on cases outside Virginia small claims or involving high-consequence issues.
assumptions: The user has a served document or reliable form details.
The workflow remains proposed and is not publicly supported.

sources.source_notes: All sources require freshness, legal, and local-practice review before supported use; the instructions are marked September 2008.

intake.data_minimization_notes: Use user summaries and only the fields printed on the warrant when needed; do not request uploads or unnecessary party information.

summary_steps: Confirm the document appears to be Virginia Form DC-402 and identify the listed court.
Organize user-confirmed warrant information and questions without selecting a factual or legal position.
Flag the listed return date for prompt official verification and provide safe resource routing.
process.process_notes: The workflow does not calculate deadlines; the served warrant, current official sources, and court information must be checked.

outputs.output_notes: Any outline remains a user-review aid, not an answer, grounds of defense, or filing-ready document.

escalation_triggers: Return date is today, imminent, unclear, or already passed.
User asks Pro-One to choose an admission, denial, defense, removal, or strategy.
Document is not clearly Form DC-402 or court jurisdiction is uncertain.
Matter involves eviction, family law, immigration, criminal exposure, domestic violence, or other high-consequence facts.
refusal_triggers: User asks Pro-One to invent facts, defenses, or evidence.
User asks Pro-One to choose a response or advise ignoring the warrant.
User asks Pro-One to sign, file, serve, or submit a document.
required_warnings: This proposed workflow provides legal information, not legal advice.
The listed return date may be important; check the served warrant and official court information promptly.
Pro-One cannot decide what factual or legal position you should take or say a document is legally sufficient.
safety.safety_notes: This is a proposed research specification and is not publicly available or supported.

review.review_notes: Official-source research completed only; no attorney, legal, privacy, or release approval is claimed.

success_criteria: The workflow stays within the identified Form DC-402 small-claims scope.
It never chooses a user response or defense.
It directs users to current official sources and flags return-date uncertainty.
known_failure_modes: Treating a non-small-claims warrant or another court procedure as in scope.
Giving a calculated deadline or response strategy.
Collecting sensitive document contents unnecessarily.
evaluation.evaluation_notes: Twelve proposed fixtures define behavior but are not reviewed or approved.
